3. Learned counsel for the respondents appeared on advance notice.

4. Learned Standing counsel appearing on behalf of respondent No.4/DDA vehemently opposed the instant petition on the ground of maintainability as well as on the factum that the petitioner has concealed certain material facts in the instant petition.

She has placed reliance upon the order dated 15th May, 2019 passed by the Division Bench of this Court in W.P.(C) 4952/2019, the copy of which has been placed before this Court during the course of the arguments.

She has referred to paragraphs 2, 3 and 5 of the said order, which is reproduced hereinbelow:-
"...2.

The narration in the petition reveals that the Petitioner No.1 Smt. Ranjit Kaur purchased Plot No.29 in Janak Park Extension from one Narender Kumar on a Power of Attorney dated 1st February 1983 and raised a house on the same.
Similarly Petitioner No.2 Smt. Jasminder Kaur purchased Plot No.27 from one Bishmber Nath on a Power of Attorney dated 22nd May 1981 and occupied the same by building a residential house.
It is further mentioned that the original owner of the two plots was one Smt. Raj Rani, whose name was duly mutated in the revenue records.
3. It is then stated that the notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act ("LAA") was issued on 6th July 1966 for the public purpose of "Planned Development of Delhi".
This was followed by declaration under Section 6 LAA issued on 5 th December 1966.
The impugned Award No.2177 th (supplementary) was passed on 10 March 1970.

sentences.text: Even where the land stands mutated in favour of the Petitioners and they have put up structures, the fact that they have joined the other residents in making a joint application for regularisation of the unauthorised colony in question, would mean that they cannot now seek a declaration that the land acquisition proceedings have lapsed.
Having elected to seek regularisation, they cannot reprobate and seek invalidation of the land acquisition proceedings.
They must follow the remedy they have opted for earlier to the logical end..."
5. It is submitted that the Division Bench of this Court has already adjudicated the similar grievance of the petitioner herein.
It is further submitted that the petitioner is aware of the order passed by the Division Bench of this Court and has not mentioned the details of the said order deliberately.
